segments.he: אות יב וזה שהזהיר התורה לגמול חסד עם העני הלוה ולבלי להיות לו כנושה. כי זה העני אשר מטה ידו עד שהוכרח לבא לידי הלוואה מאחרים. זה נמשך מהתגברות הכבד ח"ו שמשם עיקר העניות כנ"ל. ועל כן בא לידי הלוואה שהוא בחינת עבדות בחינת עבד לוה לאיש מלוה שזהו בחנית תכבד העבודה שהוא בחינת כבד שמשם עיקר העניות וההלוואות. ועל כן הזהירה התורה לישראל לחוס על הלוה לבלי להיות לו כנושה כדי להצילו ולהעלותו מבחינת עבדות מבחינת עבד לוה. רק להתנהג עצמו כבן חורין להעלותו מעבדות לחירות. כי עיקר ההלוואה הוא בשביל להחזיק ביד הלוה אולי יוכל להרחיב ידו על ידי זה שיזכה לפרנסה על ידי זה. כמו שכתוב וכי ימוך אחיך ומטה ידו עמך והחזקת בו וכו'. וכמו שפירש רש"י שם אל תניחנו ליפול אלא תחזיק בו עד שלא יפול וכו' כי העניות ח"ו הוא מהתגברות הכבד על המוח ח"ו. ועל כן זה שבא לידי עניות שהוא התגברות הכבד ח"ו על המוח ומחמת זה העניות מעביר על דעת קונו. כי דעתו מתבלבל מחמת שהתגבר ח"ו אחיזת הכבד. וכל מה שמתגבר יותרהעניות נחלש הדעת בכל פעם יותר וכמו כן מתגבר ח"ו הכבד יותר ומחמת זה העני הוא בכעס תמיד כי הכענס הוא בחינת כבד כועס שהוא בחינת עניות ומחמת שזה בתר עניא עניותא אזיל וכנ"ל. ועל כן זה שמרחם על העני ומשפיע לו פרנסה הוא מחיה נפשו ממש ויכול להציל את העני מן העיות לגמרי. כי על ידי זה שנותן לו ומחיה נפשו ומרחיב דעתו על ידי זה מתגבר הדעת על הכבד וכל מה שמתגבר הדעת נכנע הכבד שעל ידי זה מתבטל העניות כנ"ל וזהו בחינת מצוות גמילות חסדים שגדולה מן הצדקה. כי על ידי הגמילות חסדים שמלוה לו ומרחיב לו לפי שעה על ידי זה יכול להצילו מן העניות לעולם כי על ידי זה שעוזר לו ומלוה לו ומרחיב דעתו על ידי זה נכנע הכבד וכל מה שנכנע הכבד יותר נתגדל המוח יותר. וכל מה שנתגדל המוח יותר נכנע הכבד יותר עד שיכול לבטל העניות לגמרי וכנ"ל. ועל כן הזהירה התרוה על המלוה לבל יהי לו כנושה כדי להצילו מעבדות מבחינת עבד לוה וכו' כדי להצילו מבחינת התגברותה כבד שהוא בחינת תכבד העבודה בחינת עבדות כנ"ל שמשם עיק העניות וההלוואות ח"ו כנ"ל. רק להתנהג עם הלוה כאילו לא לוה ממנו כלל. ולא יהיה לו כנושה. כדי להצילו מבחינת עבדות כדי להכניע בחינת תכבד העבודה בחינת כבד מלא דם כדי לבטל הענית מישראל כי על ידי זה שאינו כנושה להלוה על ידי זה מכניע בחינת הכבד בחינת עבדות כנל ועל ידי זה יוכל הלוה לזכות להרחיב ידו ולפרוע להמלוה ולהנצל מן העניות לגמרי וכנ"ל. ועל כן קורין פרשה זו אם כסף תלוה וכו' לא תהיה לו כנושה וכו' בימי הפסח שהוא זמן חירותינו. כי זה בחינת יציאת מצרים שזכינו לצאת מעבדות לחירות שכל זה היה על ידי הכנעת הכבד לגבי המוח כנ"ל שזהו בחינת לא תהיה לו כנושה כדי להציל ישראל מבחינת עבדות להעלותם מעבדות לחירות וכנ"ל.
segments.en:
And this is the aspect of meelah on the eighth day — corresponding to the ח’it of חָמֵץ, which is broken on the eighth day through the mitzvah of meelah, as above. For the eighth day is the aspect of Alma D’Asay [the World to Come], the aspect of Binah [Understanding — the s’firah associated with the upper ה of the Divine Name], from which judgments are aroused (Zohar, VaYikra 10b), and from there the grip of the chametz derives. And judgment is only sweetened at its root (Aitz Chaim, Gate 3, ch. 11). Therefore, on the eighth day, the aspect of the chametz is sweetened and nullified completely — namely, the ח’it of חָמֵץ, as above — and then the ח’it is broken and the ה’a is made from it. That is, the ה’a of Daas, the ה’a of Avraham, which is revealed through the aspect of meelah. For there [in Binah] is the aspect of the ה’a ila’ah [the upper ה of the Divine Name], as is known.

And this is the aspect of “And on the eighth day” (VaYikra 12:3) specifically — with the ה’a hay’diah [the definite article הַ — i.e., “the eighth day,” not just “an eighth day”] — that is, the ה’a of Daas that is revealed on the eighth [day] through the mitzvah of meelah, which is the aspect of breaking the ח’it of חָמֵץ, as above. And this is the aspect of the complete nullification of chametz on the Seventh Day of Pesach, as above. [For] the Seventh Day of Pesach is the eighth day from the beginning of the nullification of chametz. For the beginning of its nullification is on Erev Pesach [the eve of Pesach], as it is written: “But on the first day you shall remove leaven” (Sh’mos 12:15) — which is Erev Pesach, called “the first.” It emerges that the Seventh Day of Pesach is the eighth day from the first day — namely, from Erev Pesach — and then is the ultimate nullification of chametz and its breaking; namely, the ח’it is broken, as above. And therefore the aspect of the mitzvah of meelah, tikkun habris, is revealed, as above, which is the aspect of the Splitting of the Sea of Reeds, as above. For the mitzvah of meelah is in the aspect of the Splitting of the Sea of Reeds. For regarding the Splitting of the Sea of Reeds it states: “And they turned back and encamped before Pi HaChiros,” etc. (Sh’mos 14:2) — that Yisrael were commanded to turn back toward the direction of Egypt, so that “Pharaoh will say of the Children of Yisrael: ‘They are confused,’” etc. (ibid. 14:3) — so that he would pursue them.

And this is the aspect of the essence of t’shuvah [repentance / return] — to rectify the blemish of the bris, as Rabainu wrote in the teaching “A drop that dies in its prayer — from where does its spirit emerge?” (Likutay Moharan I, 27). And he answered them: “Through the same [way] that it entered” (b’haynu d’a’al) — that is, they asked: from where does one extract the nitzotzos [holy sparks] that fell through the blemishing of the bris? And he answered them: “Through the same [way] that it entered” — namely, through the same path by which the nitzotzos entered and fell — namely, through the blemish of the bris. And now, when these fantasies overpower a person and he breaks his desire — through this he extracts the nitzotzos from within them; see there well. And because of this, everyone who merits t’shuvah — which is the aspect of the Exodus from Egypt, in that one goes out from the domain of the Sitra Achara into the holy — must, by Heavenly compulsion, return and go back and pass through all the places where he was at first, in order to be tested and refined in that very same matter. And this is the essence of t’shuvah, the aspect of t’shuvas hamishkal [repentance that corresponds in weight to the sin]. And through this, one extracts the nitzotzos that fell at first, in the aspect of “through the same [way] that it entered,” as above.

And this is the aspect of: “And they turned back and encamped,” etc. (Sh’mos 14:2) — that they were commanded after the Exodus from Egypt to return and go back specifically toward the direction of Egypt. And then, when the Sitra Achara sees that they are returning and drawing close to them, they say, “The way has closed upon them and they are confused” (ibid. 14:3). And then they intensify greatly with the power of all the nitzotzos that are within them, and then it is a time of great distress for Yisrael — and from this very [distress] they will be saved. For afterward, Hashem has mercy on His people and saves them, and then, specifically through this, they extract all the holy nitzotzos that were within them, as above. And this is the aspect of the Splitting of the Sea of Reeds — the depths of the sea were subdued, and Egypt and the Sitra Achara fell into them, and Yisrael then merited great wealth from the spoils of the sea — namely, they extracted all the holy nitzotzos from within them, as above.

And this is the aspect of meelah, which is tikkun habris. And the heretics challenged: If Hashem desires meelah, why did He not create man already circumcised?! — as is brought in the Midrash. And it is found in the words of Rabainu, of blessed memory, in the teaching “A prayer of Chavakkuk” (Likutay Moharan I, 19) — that one must specifically circumcise him here, in this world, in order to elevate the good from the Tree of Knowledge; see there well. For man was compelled to be created first with the orlah, and afterward to cut it and break it, in order to rectify the blemish of the bris. For all the generations come to rectify the sin of Adam HaRishon [the first man] who blemished the bris, as is brought. Therefore, they were compelled to come with an orlah, so that there would be a grip for the orlah and the Sitra Achara, and afterward one cuts it, and specifically through this one extracts the holy nitzotzos from them.

And this is the aspect of meelah on the eighth [day] — that seven days must pass over him, during which the orlah has a grip, for it is the aspect of the all-encompassing evil of the seventy nations — in order to be refined through this. And afterward, one cuts them completely, as above. And this is the essential tikkun, as above. For the seven days of orlah are the aspect of the seventy nations, which are comprised of seven. And as Rabainu wrote (Likutay Moharan I, 36) — that before one merits the revelation of Torah, one must pass through the exile of the seventy nations, as above, and be refined within them. And afterward one merits the revelation of Torah, which has seventy facets — the aspect of the seventy souls of the house of Yaakov. And this is the aspect of meelah, which is the revelation of Daas through tikkun habris, as above. And this is the aspect of the seventy chasadim [acts of lovingkindness / channels of grace] that are revealed through the mitzvah of meelah, the aspect of mal [circumcised]; see Likutay Torah.

For chesed is Daas. And this is the aspect of: “And it was on the eighth day, Moshe called to Aharon and to his sons and to the elders of Yisrael” (VaYikra 9:1). “On the eighth day” — this is Rosh Chodesh Nisan, when the redemption from Egypt begins, which is the aspect of tikkun habris. And this is the aspect of “on the eighth day” — the aspect of the mitzvah of meelah, as it is written: “And on the eighth day he shall be circumcised,” etc. (VaYikra 12:3). “Moshe called” — he who is the Daas — “to Aharon” — he is the aspect of the chasadim, for Aharon is a Kohen, a man of chesed — the aspect of Avraham, of whom it is said: “You are a Kohen forever” (Tehillim 110:4). And this is “and to his sons” — they are the aspect of limudai Hashem [those taught by G-d], where the essential revelation of the chasadim through the meelah takes place, as is brought there in the kavanos [Kabbalistic intentions].

And this is “and to the elders of Yisrael” — this is the aspect of the seventy elders, the aspect of the seventy souls of the house of Yaakov that shine through the revelation of the seventy chasadim, as above. Also, zakain [elder] is the aspect of tikkun habris, the aspect of “You shall honor the face of the zakain” — “this refers to one who has acquired wisdom,” etc., as above. And tikkun habris is through the revelation of the chasadim through the mitzvah of meelah, as above. And therefore the Kohen, who is the aspect of chesed, is commanded regarding the guarding of the bris more than others. And the Kohen Gadol [High Priest], who is a great and lofty chesed, is commanded even more regarding the guarding of the bris, and he has additional holy commandments — for tikkun habris is the aspect of the revelation of the chasadim through the subjugation of the orlah, which is the blemish of the bris, as above — and this is the aspect of meelah, as above. And therefore the Kohen Gadol wears eight garments, corresponding to the aspect of the eight days of meelah — namely, tikkun habris in its completeness that the Kohen Gadol merits, as above.

And therefore meelah is a mitzvah that Yisrael accepted with joy and they still perform it with joy. For meelah is the aspect of bittul chametz — namely, the leavening of thought — and then one can pray with power, so that one’s voice becomes thunders. And through this, joy is made, in the aspect of “and for the upright of heart — joy” (Tehillim 97:11), as all this is explained in the teaching “With Trumpets” cited above; see there well.

And this is the aspect of: “אור זָרֻע לַצַּדִּיק” — “Light is sown for the righteous” (Tehillim 97:11) — this is the aspect of tikkun habris; through this: “and for the upright of heart — joy” — as above. And therefore the final letters [of אור זָרֻע לַצַּדִּיק] spell kra [קרע], as is brought — the aspect of the Splitting (k’rias) of the Sea of Reeds, which is the aspect of meelah, as above. And this: “and for the upright of heart — joy” [ולישרי לב שמחה] — the final letters [י = 10, ב = 2, ה = 5] equal in gimatriya [numerical value] tov [טוב = 17], as is brought — the aspect of meelah, tikkun habris, as it is written: “And she saw him, that he was tov (good)” (Sh’mos 2:2; cf. Midrash Rabbah, Sh’mos ch. 1) — that he was born circumcised. And this is what the Ari z”l wrote — that through the mitzvah of meelah, one nullifies a decree of eighty years; see there. For through the joy mentioned above, one can nullify the decree, for one knows [the distinction] between before the decree and after the decree, and through this one knows how to pray and nullify it (see there well, in the teaching “With Trumpets” cited above).

And therefore, after the Song at the Sea, it states: “For I am Hashem your Healer” (Sh’mos 15:26). For the Song at the Sea and the Splitting of the Sea of Reeds is the aspect of the rectification of the mitzvah of meelah, as above, which requires healing — as our Sages of blessed memory said (M’gillah 17b): “Why was healing established [in the Shmoneh Esray] in the eighth [blessing]? Because of meelah, which was given on the eighth [day], which requires healing.” For indeed, meelah, which is the aspect of tikkun habris, through which one merits shalom [peace] (as Rabainu wrote in the teaching “A Drop” cited above), is itself a healing, as it is written there. However, because the way of shalom is to clothe itself in bitterness, as is explained there (see there) — and this is the aspect of the pain and anguish of the meelah, that one must endure bitterness and pain when one wishes to merit shalom, which is tikkun habris, the healing of the soul, the aspect of meelah — because of this, one needs afterward a healing upon the healing of shalom, in order to heal the pain of the bitterness in which the shalom clothed itself, as above. And this is the aspect of: “Heal us, Hashem, and we shall be healed” — that we pray for two healings — namely, to heal the pain of the healing, the aspect of the pain of the meelah, which is itself a healing, as above. Blessed is Hashem forever, amain and amain.

Why is meelah on the eighth [day]? So that the whole world should not be joyous while his father and mother are sad (Niddah 31b). For meelah is the aspect of the revelation of the chosam [seal] — the bris kodesh [holy covenant] — as we say [in the blessing]: “And his offspring He sealed,” etc. (Shabbas 137b). And chosam [seal] (חותם = 454) is the opposite of niddas [menstrual impurity] (נדת = 454) — for they have equal numerical value, as is brought (Aitz Chaim, Gate 35, ch. 3).

And therefore one must wait until the eighth day, when the blood of niddus [menstrual impurity] is nullified; then the chosam [seal] is revealed, as above. And this is “so that there should not be sadness” — for sadness is the aspect of the blood of niddus, as it is written: “I will greatly multiply your sorrow” (B’raishis 3:16) — this refers to the blood of niddus. And therefore the meelah is on the eighth [day], when joy is then revealed, as above — for the meelah leads to meriting joy, as above. And the joy is in the aspect of the eighth day, which is the aspect of Binah, as above. And Binah is the heart (liba), and there is the joy, as it is written: “You have placed joy in my heart” (Tehillim 4:8). And there are the thunders through which one merits joy, as above — as it is written: “And the thunder of His might — who can comprehend (yisbonain)?” (Iyov 26:14).

This teaching connects meelah (circumcision) and p’reeah (the second stage of circumcision) to the nullification of chametz (leavened bread) and s’or (leaven/sourdough) on Pesach. The core structure is:

The letter ח’it of חָמֵץ represents the “two clouds that cover the eyes” — foreign thoughts and evil fantasies. This letter has two legs reaching the ground, symbolizing the two k’lipos (husks): the orlah (foreskin = pure evil, corresponding to Esav and s’or) and the p’reeah membrane (a mixture of good and evil, corresponding to Yishmael and chametz).

When one breaks the ח’it — by cutting one of its legs — it becomes a ה’a, the letter of Daas (holy knowledge), the ה’a added to Avraham’s name when he was circumcised. Thus חָמֵץ becomes מַצָּה.

This transformation is the inner meaning of the Splitting of the Sea on the Seventh Day of Pesach — which was itself the eighth day from the start of nullifying chametz (on Erev Pesach), paralleling meelah on the eighth day. The sea split in the merit of Yosef’s tikkun habris (“The sea saw and fled” — it saw the coffin of Yosef).

The teaching further explains that t’shuvah (repentance) requires one to revisit the very places of one’s fall — “through the same way that it entered” — in order to extract the holy sparks. This is why Yisrael were commanded to turn back toward Egypt before the sea split, and why man must be born with an orlah and then cut it, rather than being created already circumcised.

Finally, the joy of meelah, the healing of shalom that comes through tikkun habris, and the relationship between chosam (seal = 454) and niddas (impurity = 454) tie together circumcision on the eighth day, the Seventh Day of Pesach, the thunders of prayer, and the ultimate joy of the heart.

aligned_segments.he: הלכה ו אות א ענים פסח על פי המאמר שאלו אתר' יוסי בן קיסמא אימתי בן דודבא וכו' עיין שם כל המאמר בליקוטיהראשון בסימן נ"ז. והכל שעל ידי נדר שנודרין איזהו דבר ומקיימין מיד על ידי זה זוכין לאומת חכמים. ועל ידי זה מתנוצצים בו אורות האבות וכו' ועל ידי זה זוכין לעונג שבת היינו אכילה בקדושה ואז יכול לפעול באכילתו מה שפועל בתענית היינו להפיך אויביו לפניו בזכות עונג שבת כמו שפועל בצום וכו'. כי על ידי הצום אויביו נופלים לפניו כי על ידי הצום מכניעין הכבד לפני המוח ונותן הממשלה להמוח היינו שמכניע הכבד כועס שהוא ראש המקטריגים שהוא עשו הוא אדום שאחיזתו בכבד מלא דם ועל ידי הצום מכניעין אותו ומתקנין את המוח ומפילים כל השונאים והמרים הנאחזין בהמקטרג הגדול הנ"ל הנאחז בכבד כועס וכו'. אבל כשזוכה לבחינת עונג שבת אז אין צריך לצום כי פועל באכילתו מה שפעל על ידי הצום היינו להשבית אויב כי אכילת שבת קודש היא וכו' אבל לרבות השלום צריכין להרבות בצדקה וכו' ויש חילוק בין השלום של תענית של חול ובין השלום של עונג שבת כי זה אין לו פה וזה יש לו פה וזהו אין בין חמץ למצה אלא מ"ש"ה"ו" נוטריקון ו"היה מ"עשה ה"צדקה ש"לום וכו' (עיין שם כל זה היטב).
aligned_segments.en: Based on the discourse "They asked Rabbi Yosai ben Kisma: When will the son of Dovid come," etc. — see there the entire discourse in the first volume, Siman 57. The general principle is that through a vow (neder) — when one vows something and fulfills it immediately — one merits emunas chachamim (faith in the Sages). And through this the lights of the Patriarchs (oros ha'Avos) are illuminated within him, etc. And through this one merits oneg Shabbos — that is, eating in holiness. And then one can accomplish through one's eating what one accomplishes through fasting — that is, to cause one's enemies to fall before him through the merit of oneg Shabbos, just as one accomplishes through fasting, etc. For through fasting one's enemies fall before him — for through fasting one subdues the liver (kavaid) before the brain (moach) and gives dominion to the brain. That is, one subdues the angry liver (kavaid ko'ais), which is the head of the accusers — which is Eisav, who is Edom, whose hold is in the liver that is full of blood. And through fasting one subdues it and rectifies the brain and causes all the enemies and adversaries who are attached to the great accuser — who is attached to the angry liver — to fall. But when one merits the aspect of oneg Shabbos, then one does not need to fast, for one accomplishes through eating what one accomplished through fasting — that is, to quell the enemy — for the eating of Shabbos is holy, etc. But to increase shalom, one must increase tz'dakah, etc. And there is a difference between the shalom of a weekday fast and the shalom of oneg Shabbos — for the former has no mouth, and the latter has a mouth. And this is: the difference between chamaitz and matzah is only a mashehu — whose letters are an acronym for "V'hayah ma'asai hatz'dakah shalom" ("And the work of tz'dakah shall be shalom") — see there well. And this is the aspect of Pesach. For the essential purpose of the Exodus from Mitzrayim was to reveal the holy emunah. For this is the essence of the Exodus — to receive the Torah, which is emunah, as it is written: "All Your commandments are emunah." As it is written: "When you bring the people out of Mitzrayim, you shall serve G-d," etc. And the essential emunah is through emunas chachamim — the aspect of: "And they believed in Hashem and in Moshe His servant." For it is impossible to believe in Hashem except when one believes in Moshe His servant — which is emunas chachamim. For His greatness is beyond investigation, and He, blessed be He, is exalted and elevated and uplifted far beyond our understanding. And it is impossible to attain the holy emunah except through the true tzaddikim, who instill the holy emunah within us. And we must believe in them and not deviate from their words to the right or to the left. And all the corruption of all the generations that were continually provoking, before matan Torah — the generation of the Flood and the generation of the Dispersion — was all through the blemish of emunas chachamim, as it is written: "He will not turn to the way of the vineyards." And Rashi explains that "vineyards" refers to the tzaddikim — they would swear not to turn to the path of the true tzaddikim who stand at the heights of the world. For in every generation there were certainly lofty, true tzaddikim — such as M'suschelach, Noach, Shem, Eiver, Chanoch, and the like. And if they had believed in them, they would have merited through them the holy emunah and the straight path of serving Hashem. And they would have been saved from the Flood and other calamities. But they lost this world and the next — all through the blemish of emunas chachamim. And so in every generation, the essential hope to merit the eternal goal — everlasting life — is through faith in true chachamim who merited to overcome their inclination, subdued their desires, turned their faces completely from the vanities of this world, chose true life, and toiled with great effort for His Name until they merited what they merited. They attained hashagas Elokus, and through the greatness of their power they can draw us close as well to Him, blessed be He. And we are obligated to believe in them — as it is written: "You shall not deviate from the word they tell you," etc. For they know how to instruct us in the path upon which we should walk and the deeds we should do. It follows that the essential thing is emunas chachamim. And this was the essence of the Exodus from Mitzrayim — to reveal the holy emunah, to reveal that Hashem is the G-d — which one merits only through emunas chachamim. And therefore at the very beginning of Moshe's mission to Yisrael, he immediately responded to Hashem: "But behold, they will not believe me and will not listen to my voice, for they will say: 'Hashem did not appear to you.'" For Moshe asked Hashem this: How can emunas chachamim be instilled in Yisrael? For he saw immediately that the essence of the redemption depended on their believing in him and fulfilling his words and following his counsel in everything he would instruct them. Therefore he immediately asked Hashem about emunas chachamim — how to instill it in them — for he thought they were far from emunas chachamim, as it is written: "But they will not believe me," etc. And this is the aspect of the three signs that Hashem gave into his hand so that they would believe in him. For Hashem commanded him to show Yisrael the punishment and the blemish that results from the blemish of emunas chachamim — so that they would strengthen themselves in emunas chachamim all the more. For the first sign was that his hand became leprous — this is the aspect of the wondrous afflictions that come upon one through the blemish of emunas chachamim, which is the aspect of "an affliction not written in the Torah" (as explained in the discourse). And therefore the sign of the affliction of leprosy was specifically in his hand — for it is specifically the hands that are blemished through the blemish of emunas chachamim (as our Rebbe wrote there, on the teaching of our Sages: "Give me your hand," etc.). And afterward He showed him the sign that the staff turned into a serpent — this is also the aspect of the blemish of emunas chachamim, which is the aspect of: "He who breaches a fence — a serpent shall bite him" — the aspect of: "Perhaps the serpent of the Rabbis has bitten him, for which there is no remedy" (as explained in the discourse). And afterward He showed the third sign — that He turned water into blood — this is also the aspect of the blemish of emunas chachamim. For through emunas chachamim, which one merits through a neder, one merits oneg Shabbos. And then the liver that is full of blood is subdued before the brain (as explained in the discourse). But when one does not merit emunas chachamim, chas v'shalom, then, chas v'shalom, the liver that is full of blood overpowers the brain, which is the aspect of water, the aspect of da'as — as it is written: "The earth shall be full of the knowledge of Hashem, as the waters cover the sea."

aligned_segments.he: וזה בחינת פסח. כי עיקר יציאת מצרים היה לגלות האמונה הקדושה שזה עיקר יציאת מצרים לקבל את התורה שהיא אמונה כמו שכתוב כל מצותיך אמונה. כמו שכתוב בהוציאך את העם ממצרים תעבדון את האלקים וכו'. ועיקר האמונה היא על ידי אמונת חכמים בחינת ויאמינו בה' ובמשה עבדו. כי אי אפשר להאמין בה' כי אם כשמאמינין במשה עבדו שהוא אמונת חכמים. כי לגדולתו אין חקר הוא יתברך מרומם ונעלה ונשא מאד מדעתינו. ואי אפר להשיג האמונה הקדושה כי אם על ידי הצדיקים האמתיים שהם מכניסין בנו האמונה הקדושה. וצריכין אנו להאמין בהם ולבלי לסור מדבריהם ימין ושמאל. וכל הקלקול של כל הדורות היו מכניסין ובאין קודם מתן תורה שהם דור המבול ודור הפלגה. הכל היה עלידי פגם אמונת חכמים כמו שכתוב לא יפנה דרך כרמים ופירש רש"י שכרמים הם הצדיקים שהיו נשבעין לבלי לפנות לדרכם של הצדקים האמתיים העומדים ברומו של עולם. כי בכל דור ודור היו בוודאי צדיקים גבוהים אמתיים כגון מתושלח ונח ושם ועבר וחנוך וכיוצא בהם ואם היו מאמיני בהם היו זוכים על ידם לאמונה הקדושה ולדרך ישרה לעבודתו יתברך. והיו ניצולים מן המבול ושאר צרות ואבדו העולם הזה והעולם הבא הכל על ידי פגם אמונת חכמים. וכן בכל דור ודור עיקר התקוה לזכות לתכלית הנצחי לחיי עד הוא על ידי אמונת חכמים אמתיים שאשר זכו להתגבר על יצרם וכפו תאוותם והפכו פניהם מהבלי העולם הזה לגמרי. ובחרו בחיים אמתיים. ויגעו וטרחו ביגיעות ועבודות גדולות לשמו יתברך עד שזכו למה שזכו. והשיגו השגת אלקות ובגודל כחם הם יכולים לקרב אותנו גם כן אליו יתברך. ואנו מחוייבים להאמין בהם כמו שכתבו לא תסור מן הדבר אשר יגידו לך וכו'. כי הם יודעין להורות לנו הדרך אשר נלך בה ואת המעשה אשר נעשה.
aligned_segments.en: And therefore the first plague of Mitzrayim was that the water turned to blood. For the Mitzrim did not believe in the prophecy of Moshe; therefore they were stricken with blood — the blood overpowered them, from where their hold was — the aspect of the liver full of blood. And now they were stricken through this itself, for all their water turned to blood — the aspect of the blood of the liver overpowering them, because they blemished emunas chachamim and did not believe in Moshe and did not want to send out Yisrael. And this is the aspect of the plague of the firstborn, through which Yisrael left Mitzrayim. And the essential element of the plague of the firstborn and the salvation of the firstborn of Yisrael was through the mitzvah of the Korban Pesach, as it is written: "And Hashem will pass through to smite Mitzrayim, and He will see the blood... and I will pass over you." For the essential Exodus from Mitzrayim was to raise up and establish the fallen emunah — which is emunas chachamim, the essential avodas Hashem, the ultimate purpose of the Exodus — as it is written: "When you bring the people out of Mitzrayim, you shall serve G-d." And the essential service of Hashem depends on emunas chachamim. For the essential exile of Mitzrayim was to rectify the blemish of the generation of the Flood and the generation of the Dispersion, as is brought — they blemished emunas chachamim, and now this needed to be rectified. And therefore the essential Exodus was through the aspect of neder, which is the aspect of peleh (wonder) — as it is written: "As in the days of your leaving from the land of Mitzrayim, I will show him wonders." Therefore the essential Exodus was through the mitzvah of the Korban Pesach, which is a neder — for all korbanos are through a neder, that one vows and consecrates the animal for the Korban Pesach and the like. And through this specifically Yisrael left Mitzrayim — for through the neder that they vowed and fulfilled with the Korb'nos Pesach that they offered, they merited to raise the fallen emunah, which is the essence of the Exodus. And through this the lights of the Patriarchs were illuminated within them — for the entire Exodus from Mitzrayim was in the merit of the Patriarchs, as mentioned in many verses. And through the neder of the Korban Pesach they merited that Hashem remembered for them the merit of the Patriarchs and their lights were illuminated within them, and through this they were redeemed. And this is what is written: "Before their fathers He performed a wonder (peleh) in the land of Mitzrayim, the field of Tzo'an" — through the above peleh, which is the neder, through this the light of the Patriarchs was remembered and illuminated within them (as this verse is explained in the discourse). And through this was the essence of the Exodus — "before their fathers He performed a wonder in the land of Mitzrayim." And through the light of the Patriarchs they merited oneg Shabbos, which is eating in holiness — which is the aspect of eating matzah, as it is written: "l'ma'an tamotz v'his'anagtem" ("in order that you shall find [satisfaction] and delight"), as is explained in the discourse. And therefore the essential beginning of the sprouting of the redemption was through the holiness of Shabbos — which is the aspect of Shabbos HaGadol that precedes Pesach. And the essential miracle of Shabbos HaGadol was that then they drew and took the Korban Pesach. That is, the essence of the redemption was through the neder that they vowed for the Korban Pesach and consecrated it. And therefore Hashem arranged that they fulfilled this specifically on Shabbos — on the Shabbos before Pesach — for through this itself, through the neder of the Korban Pesach, they merited Shabbos, which is the aspect of matzah — the essence of the Exodus, when they merited eating matzah, which is the aspect of oneg Shabbos. And all this was through the neder — the Korban Pesach that they vowed on Shabbos HaGadol, when they consecrated the Korban Pesach on the tenth of the month, as our Sages said. For through the neder one merits oneg Shabbos, which is the aspect of matzah, as explained in the discourse. And therefore through the Korban Pesach the firstborn of Yisrael were saved and the firstborn of Mitzrayim were slain. And through this was the essential redemption. For the essential b'chorah (right of the firstborn) in truth belongs only to Yisrael, who are the true firstborn of holiness — the aspect of: "My son, My firstborn, Yisrael." For Yisrael arose in thought first — as it is written: "In the beginning (B'raishis) G-d created" — for the sake of Yisrael who are called raishis (the first). And raishis is the aspect of b'chor (firstborn), who is called raishis — as it is written: "For he is the beginning of his strength." But through the sin of Adam HaRishon, when all things became intermingled and overturned and changed from their true order — this caused Eisav to emerge first, and it appeared that he was the firstborn. And therefore Ya'akov seized him to restrain him — for in truth the b'chorah does not pertain to Eisav at all, only to Yisrael alone. And therefore Ya'akov our father toiled and labored until he took the b'chorah from Eisav. And he took the b'chorah from Eisav through Eisav's craving for food — as it is written: "Pour into me, please, from this red, red stuff." And through this he sold him the b'chorah. For the b'chor is raishis, the aspect of mochin. And when one merits to break the craving for food, then the brain is elevated above the liver full of blood, which is Eisav — this is the essential aspect of the b'chorah of holiness: the elevation of the brain above the entire body. For the brain is raishis, the aspect of b'chor. But when, chas v'shalom, Eisav — who is the liver — overpowers the brain, which comes through the anger that results from the craving for food (as explained in the discourse) — this is the aspect of the b'chorah of the Sitra Achara: Eisav, the aspect of the liver full of blood, takes the b'chorah and dominion and rules over the brain, chas v'shalom. From this come all the exiles, where the nations rule over Yisrael. For Yisrael's hold is in the brain — for Yisrael arose in thought first, and thought is the brain, and they are called raishis, the aspect of raishis chochmah, the aspect of mochin. And when the nations, whose hold is in the liver full of blood — which is Eisav, through whom all the exiles come — when they rule over Yisrael, chas v'shalom, this is the aspect of the liver overpowering the brain — from whence comes "tichbad ha'avodah" ("let the work be heavy") — as is brought in the Tikkunim. And this is the essential exile of Mitzrayim — the aspect of "tichbad ha'avodah." For the essential exile of Mitzrayim was through Eisav, who is the aspect of the liver full of blood, who is the minister (sar) of Mitzrayim, as is brought. And this is why it is customary for firstborns to fast on erev Pesach — for the subduing of the liver before the brain is through fasting (as explained in the discourse). And this is what is written regarding the Korban Pesach: "With matzos and bitter herbs they shall eat it." For Hashem performed wondrous kindness with us then — and so in every generation — for to subdue the liver before the brain, which is the essence of the Exodus from Mitzrayim, the aspect of the slaying of the firstborn of Mitzrayim and the salvation of the firstborn of Yisrael — this is accomplished through fasting, through which one subdues the liver before the brain (as explained there). But at the time of the Exodus it was impossible to wait to take them out until they subdued the liver through fasting — for they were deeply sunken in the impurity of Mitzrayim (as is brought in the Writings). And if He had wanted to wait until they merited to subdue the impurity of Mitzrayim — which is the aspect of the liver full of blood — through fasting, they would have, chas v'shalom, remained stuck there. Therefore Hashem performed wondrous kindness and took them out through the aspect of peleh — through the aspect of neder, which is the Korban Pesach. Through this they merited oneg Shabbos, which is eating in holiness — the aspect of matzah, which is very great mochin, the aspect of oneg Shabbos. And through this specifically they left Mitzrayim — which is the aspect of Shabbos HaGadol before Pesach, for the essential Exodus was through the aspect of Shabbos. And they merited through eating specifically — through eating matzah, which is eating in holiness, the aspect of oneg Shabbos — to subdue through this the impurity of Mitzrayim, the aspect of the bitterness of the enslavement of the liver, the aspect of "tichbad ha'avodah." And all this they merited through the neder, which is the Korban Pesach. And this is what is written regarding Pesach: "With matzos and bitter herbs they shall eat it." For through the Pesach offering, which is a neder, one merits matzah, which is oneg Shabbos — through which one subdues the liver, the aspect of "tichbad ha'avodah" — which is the bitterness of the enslavement, the aspect of maror. And all this one merits through eating in holiness specifically — "with matzos and bitter herbs they shall eat it."

aligned_segments.he: ועל כן עיקר התחלת צמיחת הגאולה היה על ידי קדושת שבת שהוא בחינת שבת הגדול של פני פסח. ועיקר הנס של שבת הגדול הוא שאז משכו ולקחו הקרבן פסח. היינו עיקר הגאולה היה על ידי הנדר שנדרו הקרבן פסח והקדישו אותו. ועל כן סבב השם יתברך שקיימו זאת בבת דייקא דהיינו בשבת שלפני פסח כי על ידי זה בעצמו היינו על ידי הנדר של הקרבן פסח זכו לשבת שהוא בחינת מצה שהוא עיקר יציאת מצרים שאז זכו לאכילת מצה שהוא בחינת עונג שבת וכל זה על ידי הנדר שהוא הקרבן פסח שנדרו בשבת הגדל כי אז הקדישו את הקרבן פסח שהיה אז בעשור לחודש כמו שאמרו רז"ל כי על ידי הנדר זוכין לעונג שבת שהוא בחינת מצה (כמבואר במאמר הנ"ל). ועל כן על ידי הקרבן פסח ניצולו בכורי ישראל ונהרגו בכורי מצרים. ועל ידי זה היתה עיקר הגאולה. כי עיקר הבכורה באמת היא רק לישראל שהם הבכור דקדושה באמת בחינת בני בכורי ישראל. כי שיראל עלה במחשבה תחילה כמו שכתבו בראשית ברא אלקים וכו' בשביל ישראל שנקראו ראשית ראשית היא בחינת בכור שנקרא ראשית כמו שכתוב כי הוא ראשית אונו וכו'. אך על ידי חטא אדם הראשון שנתערבו כל הדברים ונתהפכו ונשתנו מסדרן האמתי. זה גרם שיצא עשו תחילה ונדמה שהוא בכור. ועל כן אחזו יעקב לעכבו. כי באמת אין הבכורה שייכה לעשו כלל רק לישראל לבדם. ועל כן טרח ויגע יעקב אבינו עד שלקח הבכורה מעשו. ועלכ ן לקח הבכורה מעשו על ידי תאוות אכלה של עשו הרשע כמו שכתוב הלעיטני נא מן האדום האדום הזה ועל ידי זה מכר לו את הבכורה כמבואר שם בפסוק. כי הבכור הוא ראשית בחינת מוחין. וכשזוכין לשבת תאוות אכילה ואזי המוח נתעלה על הכבד מלא דם שהוא עשו זה עיקר בחינת הבכורה דקדושה. שהוא בחינת התעלות המוח על כל הגוף כי המוח הוא ראשית בחינת בכור כנ"ל. אבל כשח"ו מתגבר עשו שהוא הכבד על המוח שזכה על ידי כעס הבא על ידי תאוות אכילה. (כמו שכתוב שם במאמר הנ"ל). זה בחינת בכורה דסטרא אחרא שח"ו עשו שהוא בחינת כבד מלא דם נוטל הבכורה והממשלה ומושל על המוח ח"ו. שמזה באין כל הגליות שהעובדי כוכבים מושלין על ישראל. כי ישראל אחיזתם במוח כי ישראל עלה במחשבה תחילה והמחשבה הוא המוח והם נקראין ראשית בחינת ראשית חכמה בחינת מוחין. וכשהאומות שאחיזתם בכבד מלא דם שהוא עשו שכל הגליות על ידו כמובא. כשהם שולטין על ישראל ח"ו זה בחינת התגברות הכבד על המוח ח"ו דמתמן תכבד העבודה (כמובא בתיקונים). וזה עיקר גלות מצרים בחינת תכבד העבודה כי עיקר גלות מצרים היה על ידי עשו שהוא בחינת כבד מלא דם שהוא שר של מצרים כמובא.
aligned_segments.en: And this is also the aspect of: "Pesach" is called peh sach (a mouth that speaks), as is brought. This is the aspect of the shalom that has a mouth, which one merits on Pesach — which is the aspect of matzah that one merits to eat on Pesach — the aspect of the shalom that has a mouth, as explained in the discourse. And this is the aspect of the great abundance of wealth that they merited at the time of the Exodus from Mitzrayim — as it is written: "And afterward they shall go out with great possessions." And this is the aspect of the blessing that Ya'akov took from Eisav — and all of this was because he first took the b'chorah from him — as it is written: "He took my b'chorah, and behold, now he has taken my blessing." For when the brain is elevated above the liver — which is the b'chorah of holiness — then Yisrael are nourished first, and all the shefa and blessing flows to the brain first — that is, to Yisrael. And then all the shefa and wealth belongs to Yisrael, for whose sake the world and all within it were created — all the sustenance, all the wealth, all the good of all the worlds — it all pertains to them alone, for whose sake everything was created. Only when, chas v'shalom, Yisrael blemish, and the yoke of the exile of the liver overpowers the brain, chas v'shalom — then the liver is nourished first, and they seize the shefa first, and Yisrael are nourished from the leftovers, as is brought. And therefore at the time of the Exodus, when the firstborn of the Sitra Achara was subdued and the liver was subdued before the brain — the shefa returned to its true place, to Yisrael. And they despoiled Mitzrayim — for they took from them all the wealth that truly belonged to Yisrael, for all good pertains only to Yisrael who are called raishis, who are the true b'chor for whose sake everything was created — as is explained: "B'raishis — for the sake of Yisrael who are called raishis" — the aspect of the b'chor of holiness. And therefore Ya'akov, by taking the b'chorah from Eisav, through this he took the blessing from him — as it is written: "He took my b'chorah, and behold, now he has taken my blessing." For one depends on the other. And therefore Ya'akov took the blessing from his father through the delicacies (mat'amim) he made for his father as he loved — for the mat'amim of Ya'akov are the aspect of eating in holiness, the aspect of oneg Shabbos, as it is written: "See, the fragrance of my son is like the fragrance of a field that Hashem has blessed" — which is the chakal tapuchin kadishin (holy apple orchard), as Rashi explains there — which is the aspect of the seudas Shabbos, known as chakal tapuchin kadishin. And therefore Ya'akov received the blessing on the night of Pesach, through the two kids of goats he made for his father — one he offered for Pesach and one for the chagigah. For korbanos are the aspect of neder, through which one merits oneg Shabbos and subdues the liver full of blood, which is Eisav — and one takes from him the b'chorah and the blessing and restores them to the brain, which is the b'chor of holiness, the aspect of Ya'akov. This is the essential aspect of the Exodus from Mitzrayim, which was on the night of Pesach, when Ya'akov received the blessing — all the sustenance and all the wealth, as it is written: "And G-d shall give you from the dew of heaven and from the fatness of the earth," etc. — the aspect of: "And afterward they shall go out with great possessions." And this is why we read the parashah of "Im kesef talveh" ("If you lend money") during the days of Pesach. For the essential poverty and the debts, chas v'shalom, are drawn from the above — from the overpowering of the liver over the brain, chas v'shalom. For then the nations, whose hold is in the liver in the aspect of Eisav — who is appointed over all the exiles — they rule over Yisrael, chas v'shalom, and they take all the shefa, chas v'shalom, and Yisrael are nourished from the leftovers. And through this poverty, chas v'shalom, is drawn to Yisrael. For at the time when Yisrael do the will of the Omnipresent, then is fulfilled: "There shall be no needy among you, for Hashem shall surely bless you." That is, Yisrael receive the blessing and the b'chorah from Eisav, and they rule over him — and then the needy are among others and not among you, as our Sages said. For the essential poverty, chas v'shalom, is from the overpowering of the liver over the brain — which comes through the blemish of the craving for food, which is the blemish of eating from the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil. Through this, chas v'shalom, the toil and burden of earning a livelihood is drawn — the aspect of: "In sorrow shall you eat of it"; "By the sweat of your brow shall you eat bread" — the aspect of the overpowering of the liver, "tichbad ha'avodah," the aspect of the slavery and toil of earning a livelihood. And this is the aspect of "The people spread out and gathered" — "b'shtusa" (in foolishness), as the Zohar HaKadosh explains — that due to foolishness and absence of da'as one must toil greatly and wander about for a livelihood. For the essential toil and heaviness of livelihood, chas v'shalom, is only because of the overpowering of the liver over the brain — the aspect of the blemish of da'as. And through this, chas v'shalom, "tichbad ha'avodah" intensifies — the aspect of the liver full of blood. For damim has a double meaning: Eisav, whose hold is in the liver, is a shedder of damim (blood) and also takes damim (money) and the possessions of Yisrael, chas v'shalom, when he overpowers, chas v'shalom, through the sins of Yisrael. And this is: "Whoever accepts upon himself the yoke of Torah, the yoke of government and the yoke of worldly occupation are removed from him. And whoever casts off the yoke of Torah — upon him are placed," etc. For the Torah is da'as. And therefore whoever accepts the yoke of Torah — which is the aspect of the brain overpowering the liver, the side of the body, the side of Eisav — then "when this rises, this falls," and the yoke of government and the yoke of worldly occupation are removed from him. For the dominion and kingdom of Eisav, whose hold is in the liver, is nullified — and automatically the yoke of worldly occupation is also nullified, that is, the yoke of the toil and burden of livelihood. For the essential burden of livelihood is only from the overpowering of the liver — "tichbad ha'avodah" — the aspect of slavery. And whoever casts off the yoke of Torah and da'as is weakened, chas v'shalom, and the liver overpowers — then the yoke of government and the yoke of worldly occupation are placed upon him. For one depends on the other: the yoke of worldly occupation — the burden of livelihood — is drawn from the yoke of government, the evil kingdom — the kingdom of Edom, whose hold is in the liver, from whence the essential burden of livelihood comes. But when one accepts the yoke of Torah and strengthens da'as and the liver is weakened and subdued before the brain — then the yoke of government and the yoke of worldly occupation, which are attached to the liver, are removed. And this is why the Torah warned to deal kindly with the poor borrower and not to be as a creditor to him. For this poor person, whose hand has declined until he was compelled to borrow from others — this results from the overpowering of the liver, chas v'shalom, from which the essential poverty comes. And therefore he comes to borrowing, which is the aspect of slavery — the aspect of: "a borrower is a slave to the lender" — the aspect of "tichbad ha'avodah," the aspect of the liver, from which poverty and debts essentially stem. And therefore the Torah warned Yisrael to have compassion on the borrower and not to act as a creditor — to rescue him and elevate him from the aspect of slavery, from the aspect of "a slave who borrows," and rather to conduct oneself with him as a free person — to elevate him from slavery to freedom. For the essential purpose of lending is to support the borrower — perhaps he will be able to broaden his means and merit a livelihood through this — as it is written: "And if your brother becomes poor and his hand declines with you, you shall support him." And as Rashi explains there: Do not let him fall, but hold him up before he falls. For poverty, chas v'shalom, results from the overpowering of the liver over the brain. And therefore one who comes to poverty — the overpowering of the liver, chas v'shalom, over the brain — and because of this, poverty drives him beyond the bounds of his da'as, for his da'as becomes confused because the hold of the liver has overpowered, chas v'shalom. And the more poverty intensifies, the more da'as weakens each time — and correspondingly the liver overpowers all the more. And because of this the poor person is constantly in anger — for anger is the aspect of the angry liver, which is the aspect of poverty. And because of this, "after a poor man, poverty follows." And therefore one who has compassion on the poor person and provides him a livelihood truly revives his soul and can save the poor person from poverty entirely. For by giving to him and reviving his soul and broadening his da'as — through this the da'as overpowers the liver, and the more the da'as overpowers, the more the liver is subdued, and through this the poverty is nullified. And this is the aspect of the mitzvah of g'milus chasadim, which is greater than tz'dakah — for through g'milus chasadim, lending to him and broadening his means temporarily, through this one can save him from poverty forever. For by helping him, lending to him, and broadening his da'as — the liver is subdued, and the more the liver is subdued the more the brain is enlarged, and the more the brain is enlarged the more the liver is subdued — until one can nullify the poverty entirely. And therefore the Torah warned the lender not to act as a creditor — to rescue him from slavery, from the aspect of "a slave who borrows," to rescue him from the overpowering of the liver — "tichbad ha'avodah" — the aspect of slavery, from which poverty and debts essentially come. Rather, one should conduct oneself with the borrower as if he never borrowed from him at all, and not be as a creditor to him — to rescue him from the aspect of slavery, to subdue "tichbad ha'avodah" — the aspect of the liver full of blood — to nullify poverty from Yisrael. For by not acting as a creditor to the borrower, through this one subdues the aspect of the liver, the aspect of slavery. And through this the borrower can merit to broaden his means and repay the lender and be saved from poverty entirely. And therefore we read this parashah — "If you lend money... do not be as a creditor to him" — during the days of Pesach, which is the time of our freedom. For this is the aspect of the Exodus from Mitzrayim, when we merited to leave from slavery to freedom — all of which was through the subduing of the liver before the brain. And this is the aspect of "do not be as a creditor to him" — to rescue Yisrael from the aspect of slavery, to elevate them from slavery to freedom.
